##Strategy

Let's first find the indefinite integral $\displaystyle\int\sec(2x)\tan(2x)\,dx\,$.  Then we can use the result to compute the definite integral.

##Finding the indefinite integral

To find $\displaystyle\int\sec(2x)\tan(2x)\,dx\,$, we can use U-substitution.

If we let $\blueD {u=2x}$, then ${du=2 \, dx}$ and $\maroonD{ dx=\dfrac{1}{2}\, du}$.  

So we have:


$\begin{align}\displaystyle\int\sec(\blueD{2x})\tan(\blueD{2x})\,\maroonD{dx}\,&=\displaystyle\int\sec(\blueD u)\tan(\blueD u)\, \cdot \maroonD{\dfrac12\, du}\,\\\\\\\\
&=\dfrac12\displaystyle\int \sec(u)\tan(u)\, du\,\\\\\\\\
&=\dfrac{1}{2}\cdot \sec(u)+C\\\\\\\\
&=\dfrac12\sec(2x)+C
\end{align}$

##Evaluating the definite integral

Now let's compute the definite integral:

$\begin{align}\displaystyle\int^{\pi/6}_{0}\sec(2x)\tan(2x)\,dx\, &= \dfrac12\sec(2x)\Bigg|^{\pi/6}_0\\\\\\\\
&=\dfrac{1}{2}\left(\sec\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)-\sec(0)\right)\\\\\\\\
&=\dfrac12(2-1)\\\\\\\\
&=\dfrac12\end{align}$

[[☃ explanation 1]]

options.explanation:
No, we could use U-substitution to calculate the definite integral directly. 

However, with this method, we must be sure to adjust our limits of integration.  

Here, when $\greenD{x=0}\,$, $\greenD{~u=0}~$ and when $~\goldD {x=\dfrac{\pi}{6}}\,$, $\goldD{u=\dfrac{\pi}{3}}\,$, so our limits of integration change respectively.

We can substitute to rewrite the definite integral as:

$\displaystyle\int^{\goldD{\pi/6}}_{\greenD{0}}\sec(2x)\tan(2x)\,dx\, =\displaystyle\int^{\goldD {\pi/3}}_{\greenD 0}\sec(u)\tan(u)\, \cdot \dfrac12\,du\, $ 

We can now evaluate the definite integral as shown below:

$\begin{align}\displaystyle\int^{ {\pi/3}}_{ 0}\sec(u)\tan(u)\, \cdot \dfrac12\,du\, &=\dfrac12\displaystyle\int^{ {\pi/3}}_{ 0}\sec(u)\tan(u)\, \, du\, \\
\\\\\\
&=\dfrac12(\sec(u))\Bigg|^{\large\frac{\pi}{3}}_0\\\\\\\\
&=\dfrac12\Big(\sec\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)-\sec(0)\Big) \\\\\\\\
&=\dfrac12(2-1)\\\\\\\\
&=\dfrac12
\end{align}$
